Reports of mechanical dysfunction in chronic oro-facial pain are often confused with somatisation, a condition characterized by excessive and uncontrollable symptoms that have little or no clear physical basis. In the context of chronic oro-facial pain, self-reported mechanical factors associated with this condition may be confounded by psychological factors.

Therefore, it is essential to approach these reports with caution and consider the potential overlap between mechanical dysfunction and somatisation. If you are experiencing chronic oro-facial pain and are concerned about the nature of your symptoms, consult a healthcare professional for a comprehensive evaluation and guidance on managing your condition. They can help determine whether any mechanical factors may be contributing to your symptoms and address any underlying psychological issues that may be contributing to your condition.
